rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say that King Hezekiah had five prophets, including Jonah, and selected Jonah for Nineveh; Jonah refused, citing other prophets, and left angry at the king.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أن ( حزقيال ) ملك إسرائيل كان في زمنه خمسة أنبياء منهم يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur calls the Hezekiah account remote from other Qur'anic passages and the books of the Israelites.
rows.anchor: وهذا بعيد من القرآن في آيات أخرى ومن كتب بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson of the verse does not depend on identifying the particular story behind Jonah's departure.
rows.anchor: ومحل العبرة من الآية لا يتوقف على تعيين القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies Jonah left without divine authorization, supposing that if he left the city to which he was sent, God would send someone else to its people.
rows.anchor: يقتضي أنه خرج خروجا غير مأذون له فيه من الله . ظن أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes naqdir as constrict or impose hardship; Jonah inferred that leaving would end his duty to remain with those people or deliver the message, but should have asked God what to do.
rows.anchor: أي ظن أن لن نضيق عليه تحتيم الإقامة مع القوم الذين أرسل إليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Kashshaf, Muawiya asks Ibn Abbas whether a prophet could think God lacked power; Ibn Abbas answers that the word concerns restriction, not power.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هذا من القدر لا من القدرة ) . يعني التضييق عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي
rows.claim: They explain naqdir as decree or hold accountable, from divine power; this is also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, and al-Farra and al-Zajjaj prefer it.
rows.anchor: ونقل هذا عن مجاهد وقتادة والضحاك والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the decree or accountability reading, Jonah made an erroneous judgment when he left without permission.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يكون يونس اجتهد وأخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account, the thought arose as a hasty impulse of anger after departure, before Jonah considered its implications and consequences; reports say he was naturally narrow-chested.
rows.anchor: الخروج منه بادرة بدافع الغضب عن غير تأمل في لوازمه وعواقبه ، قالوا : وكان

rows.speaker: سليمان بن المعتمر أو أبو المعتمر
rows.claim: A reading or interpretation supplies an omitted interrogative hamza: Did he think God would not constrain him? Mundhir ibn Sa'id says it was read this way.
rows.anchor: ونسب إلى سليمان بن المعتمر أو أبي المعتمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur offers the possibility that inside the whale Jonah thought God would not rescue him because escape seemed impossible under ordinary conditions; on this account the thought followed being swallowed.
rows.anchor: أنه ظن وهو في جوف الحوت أن الله غير مخلصه في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Jonah expected by ordinary causes to emigrate from his people's land and did not expect God to obstruct him, since no revelation had previously forbidden it.
rows.anchor: أنه ظن بحسب الأسباب المعتادة أنه يهاجر من دار قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah's call is repentance for negligence, haste, or mistaken judgment, and his statement magnifies his confession of self-wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: فذلك توبة صدرت منه عن تقصيره أو عجلته أو خطأ اجتهاده ، ولذلك قال : { إني كنت من الظالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb for being and the phrasing that places Jonah among wrongdoers present the quality as firmly rooted, strengthening his self-accusation.
rows.anchor: فأسند إليه فعل الكون الدال على رسوخ الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inni functions as an explanatory clause for the verb of calling.
rows.anchor: و { إني } مفسرة لفعل { نادى . }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leading with acknowledgment of God's oneness and glorification signifies that God alone governs and has power over everything.
rows.anchor: وتقديمه الاعتراف بالتوحيد مع التسبيح كنى به عن انفراد الله تعالى بالتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural darknesses refers to the darkness of night, the ocean depths, and the whale's belly.
rows.anchor: والمراد ظلمة الليل ، وظلمة قعر البحر ، وظلمة بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the plural as an intensifier for profound darkness, as in the Qur'anic movement from darknesses into light.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الظلمات مبالغة في شدة الظلمة كقوله تعالى : { يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijaba is an emphatic form of answering and here means that God answered Jonah's repentance for his lapse.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة : مبالغة في الإجابة . وهي إجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rescue coincided with the answer to his prayer; Ibn Ashur says Jonah had remained in the whale only a short hour.
rows.anchor: والإنجاء وقع حين الاستجابة إذ الصحيح أنه ما بقي في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brought about the rescue by shaping the whale's constitution so it approached shore and expelled Jonah, who then swam to land.
rows.anchor: بتقدير وتكوين في مزاج الحوت حتى خرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whale was a giant species that swallows large things whole; identifying a known species as Jonah's whale is speculation without evidence.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحوت هو من صنف الحوت العظيم الذي يبتلع الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If earth means Paradise, the verse follows naturally after the preceding passage about Paradise and also connects with the promise of the earth's diminishing from its edges.
rows.anchor: إن كان المراد بالأرض أرض الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If it means worldly land, the promise comforts believers harmed in Mecca and its vicinity: their condition will improve in this life as well as in the next.
rows.anchor: أي مصيرها بيد عباد الله الصالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad expression earth can also promise worldly dominion to Muslims as long as they remain faithful and righteous; God fulfilled the promise in both worldly and afterlife senses.
rows.anchor: على أن في إطلاق اسم الأرض ما يصلح لإرادة أن سلطان العالم

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban reports the Prophet saying God folded the earth for him, showed him its eastern and western reaches, and his community's rule would extend as far as he had seen.
rows.anchor: عن ثوبان قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read Zabur in the singular, a passive participle meaning something written, on the pattern of words for a milch or rideable camel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { في الزبور } بصيغة الإفراد

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the plural Zubur, from singular zubr meaning a written book, on the pattern of qishr and qushur.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بصيغة الجمع { زبور بوزن فعول جمع زبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority's singular reading, Zabur usually names David's book; the specific promise is notable because earlier scriptures had no general promise that the righteous would inherit the earth.
rows.anchor: فعلى قراءة الجمهور فو غالب في الإطلاق على كتاب داوود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur is David's book, preserved in the Jewish Psalms; Ibn Ashur says he cannot now identify the Psalm containing this promise.
rows.anchor: والزبور : كتاب داوود وهو مبثوث في الكتاب المسمى

rows.speaker: فويدو
rows.claim: The Italian Arabist Foido cited a Hebrew wording meaning the righteous inherit the earth as testimony that this promise existed in earlier scripture before its Qur'anic formulation.
rows.anchor: ووجدت في محاضرة للإيطالي المستعرب ( فويدو )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Hamza's plural reading, the promise was repeated across scriptures for different communities of righteous servants.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة حمزة أن هذا الوعد تكرر في الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the reminder can mean after admonition and instruction to the community: after commands, they were promised inheritance of the earth.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { من بعد الذكر } أن ذلك الوعد ورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the reminder as the Torah, the law-book given to Moses, which the Qur'an calls guidance and reminder for the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد ب { الذكر } كتاب الشريعة وهو التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Torah reading, the prepositional phrase is a settled circumstantial qualifier of Zabur, distinguishing this later promise from the earlier promise to Israel.
rows.anchor: فيكون الظرف في قوله تعالى : { من بعد الذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later promise differs from Moses' promise of the Holy Land and Israel's earlier inheritance of political power, which preceded David and was exemplified by David's kingship.
rows.anchor: وهو الوعد الذي ذكر في قوله تعالى حكاية عن موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies the later righteous community as Muslims: God fulfilled the promise through the Prophet and Companions, whose rule expanded as the Prophet had foretold.
rows.anchor: بل المراد الإيماء إلى أنه وعد وعده الله قوما صالحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative marks a break between topics or aspects, drawing attention to what follows; when it cannot serve as predicate, an omitted predicate such as this is a statement is understood.
rows.anchor: اسم الإشارة مستعمل هنا للفصل بين كلامين أو بين وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this is the more usual transition word, the verse uses the remote demonstrative to signal the elevated rank of the preceding matter.
rows.anchor: وأوثر في الآية اسم إشارة البعيد للدلالة على بعد المنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That is a fronted subject with its obvious predicate omitted, understood as a statement or the like; it resembles a writer's transition to a new subject.
rows.anchor: فاسم الإشارة مبتدأ حذف خبره لظهور تقديره

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse illustrates the common demonstrative this used to mark a transition; Ibn Ashur also cites Qur'an 38:55.
rows.anchor: وقولل زهير : هذا وليس كمن يعيا بخطبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence about honoring God's sanctities is parenthetical, attached as a new purpose to the account of God establishing Abraham at the House; it turns to preserving the foundations of Islamic monotheism.
rows.anchor: وجملة { ومن يعظم } الخ . . . معترضة عطفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun he refers to the act of honoring, implied by the verb honor.
rows.anchor: وضمير { فهو } عائد إلى التعظيم المأخوذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts to Muslims: Islam preserved the sanctities, and Muslims had performed pilgrimage and lesser pilgrimage before pilgrimage became obligatory, before the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: والكلام موجه إلى المسلمين تنبيها لهم على أن تلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sanctities are things that must be respected; respect means treating them as sacred by not violating God's commands, and the category includes all pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: والحرمات : جمع حرمة بضمتين : وهي ما يجب

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam limits the sanctities to five: the Sacred Mosque, House, land, and month, and a person while in consecration.
rows.anchor: وعن زيد بن أسلم : الحرمات خمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur takes the category more broadly to include sacrificial animals, garlands, the sacred site, and other pilgrimage acts and observances.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الحرمات يشمل الهدايا والقلائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission for livestock follows the mention of livestock and sanctities, invalidating pagan self-imposed bans on animals such as bahira, sa'iba, wasila, and hami described in the Cattle chapter.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر آنفا بهيمة الأنعام وتعظيم حرمات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is for livestock prohibitions recited in Qur'an 6:145 and in the earlier Meccan chapter of the Bee.
rows.anchor: واستثني منه ما يتلى تحريمه في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense being recited covers what had already been recited before this sura and remains recited, as well as later revelation such as the verse denying pagan animal categories.
rows.anchor: وجيء بالمضارع في قوله : إلا ما يتلى عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to avoid idols is stated as a continuing obligation, like the command to believe in God and His messenger.
rows.anchor: والأمر باجتناب الأوثان مستعمل في طلب الدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to avoid idols is an inserted clarification to avoid what is outside God's sanctities, namely idols.
rows.anchor: وفرع على ذلك جملة معترضة للتصريح بالأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: False speech includes lying about God by labeling permitted things such as blood or meat dedicated to another forbidden, and forbidden things such as bahira and sa'iba lawful.
rows.anchor: واجتناب الكذب على الله بقولهم لبعض المحرمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is called al-Mu'minun by association with the believers whose success it announces at the opening.
rows.anchor: فالأول على اعتبار إضافة السورة إلى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mu'minun can instead quote the exact word that opens the sura and identify it by that wording.
rows.anchor: والثاني على حكاية لفظ { المؤمنون } الواقع أولها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports that Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib saw the Prophet pray at the Ka'ba during the conquest, begin this sura, cough at its mention of Moses or Jesus, and bow.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن السائب قال : حضرت رسول الله يوم الفتح

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن السائب
rows.claim: Abu Dawud reports Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib saying the Prophet led dawn prayer in Mecca with this sura, coughed at the mention of Moses and Aaron or Moses and Jesus, then cut the recitation short and bowed.
rows.anchor: روى أبو داود : ( عن عبد الله بن السائب

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Common names include Qad Aflaha and Surat al-Falah; al-Utbiyya cites Ibn al-Qasim relating Malik's grandfather's Uthman-era mushaf and its notation for the sura, in contrast to the reading at 23:85.
rows.anchor: ومما جرى على الألسنة أن يسموها سورة ( قد أفلح )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan by consensus; the claim that its mention of zakah makes it Medinan is mistaken.
rows.anchor: وهي مكية بالاتفاق . ولا اعتداد بتوقف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah here means charity, not the later fixed levy on specified wealth, so its mention does not date the sura to Medina.
rows.anchor: فالزكاة المذكورة فيها هي الصدقة لا زكاة النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an uses zakah for charity in Meccan Fussilat, and says Isma'il commanded his household to pray and give zakah before the fixed levy existed.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق الزكاة على الصدقة مشهور في القرآن ، قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated relative construction presents each trait as a cause of success because each signals firmly rooted faith; the list need not exhaust piety or every cause of success.
rows.anchor: وبتكريره للإيماء إلى وجه فلاحهم وعلته ، أي أن كل خصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with condemned people who did not pray, feed the poor, or heed Judgment shows the traits' causal relevance, though an enumeration need not be exhaustive.
rows.anchor: كما كانت أضدادها كذلك في قوله تعالى { ما سلككم في سقر قالوا لم نك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushu is fear that produces reverence; directed to God, it entails piety and contributes to success.
rows.anchor: وهو خوف يوجب تعظيم المخوف منه ، ولا شك أن الخشوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushu belongs to the heart rather than being a formal act of prayer and can exist outside prayer, but is singled out in prayer because prayer especially stirs it.
rows.anchor: إذ الخشوع محله القلب فليس من أفعال الصلاة ولكنه يتلبس به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the most fitting state for khushu because it is intimate address to God, making the worshipper feel before Him; this is foundational conduct toward the Creator.
rows.anchor: ولأن الخشوع لما كان لله تعالى كان أولى الأحوال به حال الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This attribute comes first after faith because prayer is the foremost setting for khushu, praising believers first for faith and then humility before God.
rows.anchor: ولهذا الاعتبار قدم هذا الوصف على بقية أوصاف المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting in their prayer before humble emphasizes close attachment to prayer; the possessive construction signals strong connection, unlike saying they are humble whenever they pray.
rows.anchor: وتقديم في صلاتهم } على { خاشعون } للاهتمام بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence conveys lasting, stable khushu as a character trait; a verbal expression such as they humbled would not, and the wording is concise without losing force.
rows.anchor: ما تدل عليه الجملة الاسمية من ثبات الخشوع لهم ودوامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakah originally denotes purification of the self from vices; it was extended to spending wealth for God because this purifies the donor or increases the donor's wealth, naming effect for cause.
rows.anchor: أصل الزكاة أنها اسم مصدر ( زكى ) المشدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here zakah denotes the money given, using the verbal noun for its resulting object; the construction with doers requires an object, as in the command to take charity that purifies.
rows.anchor: وأطلقت على نفس المال المنفق من إطلاق اسم المصدر على المفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object cannot be the verbal noun itself: a verb cannot take its own cognate verbal noun as object in ordinary Arabic, unlike an object or result meant by doing this.
rows.anchor: وأما المصدر فلا يكون مفعولا به لفعل من مادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied action is giving zakah, equivalent to they give zakah; there is no need to supply a separate word for performance.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالفعل هنا الفعل المناسب لهذا المفعول وهو الإيتاء

rows.speaker: محمد بن بشير الخارجي
rows.claim: The broader word doers is chosen because this root is widely used for doing good; Muhammad ibn Bashir al-Khariji's poem illustrates spending wealth and undertaking noble acts.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن بشير الخارجي : إن تنفق المال أو تكلف مساعيه

rows.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
rows.claim: A poem attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt uses zakah for charitable giving, but Ibn Ashur doubts its attribution because this sense may derive from Qur'anic terminology.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الاعتبار جاء ما نسب إلى أمية بن أبي الصلت

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says scholars do not treat Umayya's poetry as authoritative evidence against the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة في كتاب ( الشعر والشعراء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn Ashur's reading of zakah as the object of doers, lam reinforces a weak derived verb that follows its object.
rows.anchor: واللام على هذا الوجه لام التقوية لضعف العامل

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم والراغب
rows.claim: Abu Muslim and al-Raghib take lam as causal, understand zakah as purification of the soul, and supply righteous deeds as the omitted object of doers.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم والراغب : اللام للتعليل وجعلا الزكاة تزكية النفس

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls zakah a verbal noun meaning the giver's act of giving zakah and says doer naturally takes such a verbal-noun complement.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الكشاف ) أن الزكاة هنا مصدر وهو فعل المزكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur says al-Kashshaf privileges formal grammar to explain the construction, and its analysis depends on an unnecessary implied noun or verbal-noun reading.
rows.anchor: فغلب جانب الصناعة اللفظية على جانب المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakah frequently occur together in Qur'an; here avoiding frivolity separates them for a thematic reason discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وعقب ذكر الصلاة بذكر الزكاة لكثرة التآخي بينهما في آيات القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving zakah is proper conduct toward people in need and belongs to ethics governing the use of wealth.
rows.anchor: وهذا من آداب المعاملة مع طبقة أهل الخصاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated relative pronoun and fronting of the object follow the same construction explained for the preceding qualities.
rows.anchor: والقول في إعادة الموصول وتقديم المعمول كما تقدم آنفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This quality comprises two major virtues: faithfully returning trusts and keeping covenants.
rows.anchor: هذه صفة أخرى من جلائل صفات المؤمنين تنحل إلى فضيلتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A trust is often a valuable object privately left with someone thought reliable; its value and lack of witnesses tempt the trustee to retain or deny it, so returning it is a branch of faith.
rows.anchor: فهي لنفاستها قد تغري الأمين عليها بأن لا يردها

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports the Prophet saying trust settled deep in people's hearts, was learned from Qur'an and Sunna, then was withdrawn during sleep until people rarely returned trusts; apparent competence no longer signaled faith. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة بن اليمان قال ( حدثنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakt is a dark mark on date skin; majal is a raised swelling on thin skin, likened to grape skin, from fire or repeated handwork.
rows.anchor: الوكت : سواد يكون في قشر التمر . والمجل : انتفاخ في الجلد الرقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith's mustard-seed measure means the trust people place in someone, not faith inside him; only a gullible person would entrust him.
rows.anchor: هو مصدر آمنه ، أي وما في قرارة نفسه شيء من إيمان الناس إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur previously discussed trusts under the verse commanding that they be delivered to their owners.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على الأمانة في قوله تعالى : { إن الله يأمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural reflects the many kinds of trusts and people entrusted with keeping them, explicitly emphasizing generality.
rows.anchor: وجمع { الأمانات باعتبار تعدد أنواعها

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the word in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : لأماناتهم } بصيغة الجمع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the singular amanah as a verbal noun, comparable to the wording for humility in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن كثير { لأمانتهم } بالإفراد باعتبار المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant is a commitment between two or more parties about how they will treat one another.
rows.anchor: والعهد : التزام بين اثنين أو أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name covenant reflects both parties pledging by God, who oversees the agreement and can hold them accountable for breach.
rows.anchor: وسمي عهدا لأنهما يتحالفان بعهد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur previously discussed the covenant under the verse about those who break God's covenant after its binding.
rows.anchor: وتقدم عند قوله تعالى : { الذين ينقضون عهد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping covenants is a great virtue showing nobility and resolve; people may betray burdensome duties for another's benefit out of greed or weak resolve.
rows.anchor: والوفاء بالعهد من أعظم الخلق الكريم لدلالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says a covenant will be called to account, reinforcing the moral weight of keeping it.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { وأوفوا بالعهد إن العهد كان مسؤولا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Watching over means preserving something from loss and repairing what decays; it also describes tending livestock or people and, metaphorically, treating people well.
rows.anchor: والرعي : مراقبة شيء بحفظه من التلاشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Watching over a trust means preserving it, with return to its owner as the purpose; watching over a covenant is keeping it in view whenever relevant.
rows.anchor: فرعي الأمانة : حفظها ، ولما كان الحفظ مقصودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted phrase and repeated relative pronoun follow the pattern of the preceding qualities.
rows.anchor: والقول في تقديم { لأماناتهم وعهدهم } على { راعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusts and covenants are joined because a person who makes a covenant entrusts the other party to fulfill it.
rows.anchor: والجمع بين رعي الأمانات ورعي العهد لأن العهد كالأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This trait follows zakah because wealth given is God's trust, called the right of God, the right of wealth, and the right of the poor.
rows.anchor: وذكرهما عقب أداء الزكاة لأن الزكاة أمانة الله عند الذين أنعم عليهم بالمال
